{{Short description|Australian ornithologist, mammalogist, and herpetologist}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=July 2019}}
'''John Casimir Zichy Woinarski''' is an Australian [[Ornithology|ornithologist]], [[Mammalogy|mammalogist]], and [[Herpetology|herpetologist]].  He was awarded the 2001 [[Eureka Prize]] for Biodiversity Research.  In the same year he was the recipient of the [[D. L. Serventy Medal]], awarded by the [[Royal Australasian Ornithologists Union]] for outstanding published work on birds in the Australasian region.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2001 |title=D. L. Serventy Medal: Citation |url=https://birdlife.org.au/documents/AWR-serventy-medallists-1991-2020.pdf |url-status=dead |journal=Emu |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201002024627/https://birdlife.org.au/documents/AWR-serventy-medallists-1991-2020.pdf |archive-date=2020-10-02 |access-date=2025-04-01 |via=Birdlife Australia}}</ref>

Woinarski is currently Professor in the Research Institute for the Environment and Livelihoods, a part-time position at [[Charles Darwin University]], in [[Darwin, Northern Territory|Darwin]], [[Northern Territory]]. Much of his work has been focused on the conservation of threatened species and he has extensively published work on the responses of biodiversity to fire.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.environment.gov.au/biodiversity/bushfire-recovery/expert-panel|title=Australian Commonwealth, Department of Agriculture Water and Environment, Wildlife and threatened species bushfire recovery Expert Panel|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907020152/https://www.environment.gov.au/biodiversity/bushfire-recovery/expert-panel|archive-date=7 September 2020|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref> He is a co-author of ''The Action Plan for Australian Mammals 2012''.<ref>{{cite book|title=The Action Plan for Australian Mammals 2012|format=PDF|isbn=9780643108745|url=https://www.publish.csiro.au/book/7010/#details|date=June 2014|publisher=CSIRO|first1=John|last1=Woinarski|first2=Andrew|last2=Burbridge|first3=Peter|last3=Harrison}}</ref>

In February 2019, speaking about the confirmed extinction of the [[Bramble Cay melomys]], considered the only mammal endemic to the [[Great Barrier Reef]] and the first documented extinction of a mammal species due to [[climate change]], he said that its loss was foreseeable and preventable. It had been known for years that its position was precarious, and he believed that its loss is at least partly due to under-funding for conservation programs and the fact that it was not an animal charismatic enough to garner much public attention.<ref name=ABC>{{cite web|website=Triple J Hack|publisher=Australian Broadcasting Corporation|date=20 February 2019|url=https://www.abc.net.au/triplej/programs/hack/bramble-cay-melomys-first-climate-change-mammal-extinction/10830080|first=James|last=Purtill|accessdate=21 February 2019|title=An Australian rodent has become the first climate change mammal extinction}}</ref>

After the [[2019–20 Australian bushfire season]] Woinarski became a member of the Australian Commonwealth’s Wildlife and threatened species bushfire recovery Expert Panel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.environment.gov.au/biodiversity/bushfire-recovery/expert-panel|title=Australian Commonwealth, Department of Agriculture Water and Environment, Wildlife and threatened species bushfire recovery Expert Panel|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200907020152/https://www.environment.gov.au/biodiversity/bushfire-recovery/expert-panel|archive-date=7 September 2020|url-status=live|df=dmy-all}}</ref>

In May 2020 the Federal Court of Australia accepted Woinarski's contributed expert opinion for the protection of some important forests in South Eastern Australia, being the threatened natural habitat of Australia's iconic [[Greater Glider]] and the [[Leadbeater’s Possum]].<ref>{{cite web|website=Federal Court of Australia|date=27 May 2020|url=https://www.judgments.fedcourt.gov.au/judgments/Judgments/fca/single/2020/2020fca0704/summary/2020fca0704-summary?fbclid=IwAR1tUoVejGqTQp3BugJWAf-2V_5bZ-XGXSpkS1z6ykguSOkVMjiIb7_LXBw|accessdate=27 May 2020|title=Friends of Leadbeater's Possum Inc v VicForests (No 4) [2020] FCA 704}}</ref>

== Awards and recognition ==
Woinarski was awarded a Christensen Research Fellowship in 1987.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Woinarski, John Casimir Zichy – Person |url=https://www.eoas.info/biogs/P003212b.htm |access-date=2025-04-01 |website=Encyclopedia of Australian Science and Innovation |language=en-gb}}</ref> He won three awards in 2001, the [[Eureka Prizes|Eureka Prize]] for Biodiversity Research, the [[Australian Natural History Medallion]] and the Serventy Medal.<ref name=":0" /> In 2008 he was recognised for his work in the Northern Territory by the awards, NT Chief Minister's Award for Research and Innovation and the NT Tropical Knowledge Research and Innovation Award.<ref name=":0" /> He was elected a Fellow of the [[Royal Zoological Society of New South Wales]] in 2017.<ref name=":0" />
